name: PT Barito Pacific Tbk

frontmatter.title: Barito Pacific: a thin premium over the discounted parts
frontmatter.summary: Barito Pacific is the Prajogo Pangestu group's apex holding company, owning Chandra Asri Pacific and Barito Renewables. The parts are worth Rp1,139 a share after the 30% holdco discount; the Rp1,235 price is 24.1% below the undiscounted parts but 1.08x the discounted house value. The konglo lens gives a Rp1,411 target, a 14.6% return: ADD.
thesis: An apex holding company over two listed legs: Chandra Asri Pacific in petrochemicals, refining and infrastructure at its published house target, and Barito Renewables in geothermal at its unpublished house target [S8, S15, S16].

The parts are worth Rp1,139 a share after the 30% holdco discount; the Rp1,235 price is 24.1% below the undiscounted parts but 1.08x the discounted house value — a thin premium to what we think the group is worth even though it sits below the gross assets [S8, S15, S16].

BREN's house target sits far above its house fundamental, so most of BRPT's marked value is a regime premium we cannot underwrite as fundamental; at BREN's fundamental the discounted parts roughly halve [S16].
FY2025 profit is a non-cash bargain-purchase gain; strip it and the group is loss-making at the parent level, which is why no earnings multiple carries weight in the valuation [S8].

The annual report shows the controller at 71.4% and the public at 28.6%; the exchange registry free float the konglo lens uses is 27.0%, a different measure that clears the fifteen per cent floor, and the name is not on the HSC list [S8, S12, S13].
The konglo lens reads the price as 1.08x the discounted fundamental value, keeps part of that premium for a year, and sets a Rp1,411 target — a 14.6% return, hence the ADD rating [S10, S11].

catalysts.event: MSCI opened a consultation on reclassifying Indonesia to Standalone Market status; feedback runs to 30 April 2027 and the decision is due by 30 June 2027 [S10]
Barito Pacific announced a share buyback programme [S4]
First free-float deadline under the raised fifteen per cent minimum [S11]
MSCI decision on Standalone status for Indonesia [S10]

blocks.text: Barito Pacific is the apex holding company of the Prajogo Pangestu group. It controls two listed legs — Chandra Asri Pacific (TPIA), the petrochemicals, refining and infrastructure arm, and Barito Renewables (BREN), the geothermal generator — with smaller unlisted property and logistics interests around them [S8]. We initiate at ADD with a twelve-month target of Rp1,411 against a last price of Rp1,235, a total return of 14.6%.

The call turns on the marks, not on the operating cycle. After the 30% holdco discount the parts are worth Rp1,139 a share: that is the discounted house value, not the gross asset value. Grossed up for the same discount, the undiscounted parts are higher, and at Rp1,235 the shares trade 24.1% below them — so the tape is not above the gross assets. It is 1.08x the discounted house value, which is the correct base for the thesis: a thin premium to what we think the group is worth after the holdco discount, not a discount to it [S8, S16]. The Director ruling of 29 October 2026 settles the sibling marks — TPIA at its published house target from the TPIA coverage report [S15], BREN at its unpublished house target [S16], neither at market — and the resulting discounted parts value is what the model uses.

The BREN mark is the swing factor. Its house target stands far above its house fundamental, and at the fundamental the discounted parts value roughly halves, with the exact figures recorded in the assumptions file [S16]. The base keeps the target because the ruling fixes it until BREN publishes; the reader should treat most of the discounted parts value as BREN's regime premium rather than as fundamental worth. The sensitivity is not symmetrical: halving the discounted parts moves the twelve-month target by far less, because the konglo lens anchors the target to today's price.

The konglo lens then sets the twelve-month number. The price is 1.08x the discounted fundamental value — a thin premium — and the lens keeps part of that gap for a year rather than closing it: fundamental twelve-month value is Rp1,331 and the target is Rp1,411 [S10, S11]. The target sits above today's price because the forward roll of fundamental value outpaces the premium compression the lens assumes; after the price refreshed to the latest confirmed close the return is 14.6%, hence ADD.

Three things move the value from here: the petrochemical and refining spread cycle at Chandra Asri; the MSCI and free-float calendar that sets the flow backdrop for concentrated-ownership names; and the path of BREN's own valuation work, which would replace the unpublished mark if it publishes [S8, S10, S11].

Holding companies over listed subsidiaries are common on the Indonesia Stock Exchange: the family vehicle holds control stakes, the listed operating arms raise capital, and investors routinely compare the parent's market value with the value of its stakes. A gap between the two is normal rather than an anomaly, and its direction can be either a discount or a premium depending on flows and control.

Barito Pacific is a holding company. Its operating value sits in its subsidiaries rather than in a trading business of its own [S8]. The group is organised around two listed legs: petrochemicals and refining through Chandra Asri Pacific (TPIA), and geothermal energy through Barito Renewables (BREN), with property, logistics and other smaller interests around them [S8].

The petrochemical leg is the larger by revenue. Chandra Asri operates olefins, polyolefins, styrene monomer and butadiene production, and in 2025 it acquired an interest in a Singapore refinery, extending the group into refining and, subsequently, fuel retail [S8]. That acquisition is why group revenue and costs both step up sharply: the refinery is a high-throughput, low-margin business that changes the consolidated revenue base without lifting the margin proportionally [S8, S7]. Chandra Asri also owns sixty per cent of Chandra Daya Investasi (CDIA), the infrastructure arm that runs power, water, ports and storage for the same industrial estate, so the petrochemical leg carries an infrastructure business inside it rather than beside it [S8].

The energy leg is Barito Renewables, which the group controls through BREN and which operates Star Energy Geothermal's geothermal fields [S8]. BRPT's ownership of BREN is 66.7%, and its effective ownership of Chandra Asri Pacific is 38.5% [S8].

The controlling shareholder is the Prajogo Pangestu family through the Barito group: the chairman's direct stake is 71.4% and the public holds 28.6% [S8]. The group's stated strategy is regional expansion of the petrochemical and energy businesses while maintaining sound governance at the portfolio-company level [S5].

The revenue and profit mix follows the same split. On a consolidated basis the petrochemical and refining leg dominates the top line, because a refinery processes large volumes at thin unit margins, while the geothermal leg contributes steadier, higher-margin revenue from contracted generation [S8]. Property, logistics and the remaining activities are small relative to the two legs and are not the swing factor in group earnings [S8].

Read as a portfolio rather than an operating company, the parent's job is capital allocation: choosing which leg to fund, when to bring in partners — as it did at Chandra Asri with Glencore and with the fuel-retail acquisition — and how much cash to upstream [S8]. That is why governance and group structure, not the parent's own trading, decide the value that reaches shareholders [S8].

The operating footprint is domestic at its base and increasingly regional at its edge: the petrochemical and geothermal assets are in Indonesia, while the refining and fuel-retail acquisitions extended the group into Singapore and the wider region [S8]. The parent's own head office functions — treasury, capital allocation and group governance — are the activities that sit directly at Barito Pacific rather than inside a leg, which is why the holdco-level cost base and debt are the bridge items between the sum of the parts and the value a parent shareholder captures [S8].

The petrochemical industry is cyclical and capital-intensive, and the group's position is that of a large domestic producer exposed to regional olefin and polymer spreads [S8]. The refining and retail assets acquired in Singapore broaden the group's footprint across Southeast Asia but tie it more tightly to refining margins and fuel-retail economics than to the polymer cycle alone [S8].
The geothermal business is a regulated, contracted, low-variable-cost generator — the more stable of the two legs, and the one the group added to balance the petrochemical cyclicality [S8].

The house macro deck reads the regime as cautious, with balance-of-payments pressure and Indonesian rate-sensitive domestic demand on avoid; for a dollar-indebted petrochemical group that argues against the premium the tape pays to our discounted house value [S7]. We translate the dollar accounts at the deck's spot rate of Rp18,138/USD rather than its FY2027E rate of Rp18,350/USD, so the rupiah target is stated on the spot cross; marking at the forecast would lift the rupiah value by the FX gap [S7, S8].

Competitive positioning is best read through the group structure rather than at the parent: the parent's economics are the economics of its two listed legs. The barriers that matter are the scale of the petrochemical complex, its integration into refining, and the resource and licensing position of the geothermal fields [S8].

External influences are the petrochemical spread cycle, the rupiah and the regional refining margin environment, and — decisively for an apex holdco — Indonesian capital-markets policy toward concentrated-ownership names [S8]. The free-float rule now requires fifteen per cent with staged deadlines from 31 March 2027, and MSCI is consulting on moving Indonesia to Standalone status with a decision due by 30 June 2027 [S10, S11]. For a name whose marginal price is set by flows in a thin float, those rules matter more than the polymer spread over a twelve-month horizon.

Five forces, read at the group level: buyer power is moderate, since petrochemical products trade in liquid regional markets where no single customer sets the price, while geothermal output is sold under long-term contracts to a state utility, which concentrates buyer power there [S8]. Supplier power is meaningful because feedstock costs are set by global oil and gas prices the group cannot influence [S8]. The threat of substitutes is real in petrochemicals, where competing producers and recycled feedstock cap pricing power, and low in geothermal, where the resource is fixed [S8]. Rivalry is intense in petrochemicals and regional refining, where the group competes with larger integrated producers, and limited in geothermal, where licences and fields gate entry [S8]. Entry barriers are highest where capacity, integration and licences matter — the petrochemical complex and the geothermal resource — which is also where the group's moat sits [S8].

The group's market position is that of a large domestic champion in petrochemicals with a broadening regional refining and retail footprint, and a leading listed geothermal developer — a leader in its home market rather than a global price-setter [S8].

The regulation that matters most to the value of the parent is not industry regulation at all, it is capital-markets regulation. The exchange's treatment of concentrated-ownership names — the raised minimum free float with its staged deadlines and the removal of high-concentration names from the headline indices — together with the possibility of MSCI removing Indonesia from its emerging-market benchmarks, determines the flow backdrop against which this stock trades, and therefore how quickly any fundamental under-valuation or over-valuation is closed [S10, S11, S13]. Industry regulation, by contrast, is a second-order influence: petrochemical capacity, the CDIA infrastructure concessions and geothermal licensing shape the legs' own long-run economics but do not set the parent's discount or premium [S8].

Petrochemical producers convert oil- and gas-derived feedstock into olefins and polymers, and profitability hinges on the spread between feedstock and product prices rather than on volumes alone. Geothermal generators rely on long-term contracts and fixed resources, so their revenue is far less volatile than that of a chemical producer.

Group revenue stepped up sharply with the Chandra Asri refining acquisition: FY2025 revenue was US$7,630.7m, against US$2,387.0m in FY2024 [S8]. The step-up is an acquisition effect, not organic growth. The filed cost of revenues is 7,378 USD m and the filed gross profit is 253 USD m, which is what a reader sees first [S8]. The engine's cost-of-goods line is US$7,082.8m, because the filed figure already contains the depreciation that the same annual report reports separately at 309 USD m; the two presentations therefore produce the same EBIT of US$-204.8m and the same EBITDA of US$104.0m [S8].

That bridge matters for reading the trough. On the filed presentation the gross margin is a single-digit number, but it is after a depreciation charge that sits inside cost of revenues; on a cash-cost basis the margin is wider, and the segment note's result is 548 USD m [S8]. FY2025 EBITDA of US$104.0m is a genuine trough, but not because of a full year of the refinery: the Singapore refinery was consolidated from its 21 April 2025 completion, so FY2025 carried only a part-year and FY2026 is its first full year [S8]. The group's operating result barely cleared its depreciation, which is why the forecast is anchored on the H1-2026 actual rather than on this trough.

Reported profit is not a guide to that operating result. Profit for the year was 1,616 USD m and parent net profit was 489.8, but the statement includes a non-cash gain from a bargain purchase of 1,868 USD m [S8]. Strip the gain and the group is loss-making at the parent level: operating cash flow of 310 USD m is ahead of normalised earnings, so accruals are negative once the non-cash item is removed [S8]. We classify this as an optics-class effect to disclose, not a manipulation flag — the gain is disclosed, audited and non-cash — but it makes the reported P/E meaningless.

The forecast is anchored on the latest actual, not on the FY2025 trough. H1-2026 revenue was US$5,685.9m and raw materials and production costs were US$4,471.3m [S7], a cash gross margin of 21.4%; we hold that margin across the forecast because no source discloses a refinery-only margin or a spread path, and the house method rules out an unsourced squeeze [S8, S7]. Selling costs and G&A were US$41.6m and US$129.7m [S7], and total operating costs including depreciation are held at the H1 ratio of 6.9% of revenue [S7]. Annualising the H1 run-rate — no archived source explains a second-half decline — gives FY2026 revenue of US$11,371.9m, operating costs of US$788.8m and EBITDA of US$2,086.7m, an EBITDA margin of 18.3% [S7, S8]. The margin path is flat from FY2027E at 21.4% to FY2035E at 21.4%; the bear scenario, not the base, carries the spread compression. The FY2025-to-FY2026 step is the largest calibration item and reflects the acquisition's first full year, not an unsourced margin assumption.

Interest and minorities are why parent earnings stay thin even as EBITDA recovers. FY2025 interest on financial liabilities not classified as fair value through profit or loss was US$379.3m, the LK's finance-cost-note interest line before bank charges, lease interest and deferred-financing amortisation, which together take total finance costs higher [S8, F43]. The forecast carries US$634.7m on the enlarged debt stack, so parent net profit is US$276.0m on the recovered operating base [S8, S7]. The large minority share — US$1,125.8m of FY2025 net profit — absorbs most of the operating result before it reaches the parent [S8]. The forecast parent profit is therefore a fraction of group EBITDA, and FY2025 parent profit is a bargain-gain artefact; this is why the valuation does not capitalise earnings.

The balance sheet carries meaningful leverage at the consolidated level. Consolidated net debt was US$4,543.2m at the end of FY2025, and most of it sits inside the listed legs — TPIA's refinery and chemical facilities, and BREN's geothermal project debt [S7, S8]. That is why the valuation deducts only the parent's own debt, not the consolidated figure: the listed legs are marked at their equity values, which already carry their debt, so netting consolidated debt again at the holdco level would double-count it [S7, S8]. The parent-only deduction is built from the Company's own balance-sheet items in the H1-2026 LK: its shelf-registration bonds [F11-F16], its two bank term loans [F17, F18], and its nil short-term bank loan at the half-year date [S7]. Parent-only cash is not separately disclosed in either statement, so the deduction is stated as the Company's own gross interest-bearing debt rather than a derived net figure [S7, S8].

On cash flow, the pattern to watch is the gap between EBITDA and free cash flow, because a refining and petrochemical business consumes working capital as throughput rises [S8]. FY2025 free cash flow was US$-1,005.1m, weighed down by the acquisition, the working-capital build and capital expenditure of 915 USD m [S8]. The group's capital allocation has been expansionary, so capex and financing flows are large relative to the parent's own resources [S8].

This is a holding company over listed stakes, so the primary method is a sum-of-parts [S8]. The house holdco card governs: listed stakes are marked at house value, holdco debt is deducted, and the resulting discount is treated as the base rate rather than as the opportunity. We do not use an earnings multiple, because FY2025 parent profit exists only because of the bargain-purchase gain, so a multiple on it capitalises a one-off [S8, F23]. We do not use a book multiple either: the same gain inflated book value, and the pre-acquisition five-year average is not a post-acquisition benchmark [S8]. That leaves the sum-of-parts as the only honest method, carrying 100% of the weight. This is a single-method valuation and we state the limitation: the DCF shown below is a sanity cross-check with zero weight, not an independent value, and the earnings and book multiples are unusable on a bargain-gain-distorted denominator [S8].

The marks are the Director ruling of 29 October 2026 [S16]. TPIA is carried at its published house target from the TPIA coverage report [S15] and BREN at its unpublished house target [S16]; neither is carried at market. The stakes themselves are from BRPT's annual report [S8, F9, F10]. CDIA is not a separate line because it sits inside TPIA's own valuation, and TPIA's house target already reflects that ownership; marking CDIA again at BRPT level would double-count it [S15]. The parent deduction is built from the Company's own debt items in the H1-2026 LK [S7, F11-F18], as set out in the financial section, and is gross parent debt with no parent cash netted. The consolidated associates and joint ventures of US$760.7m on the interim balance sheet sit inside the operating legs whose equity marks we use; the residual unlisted property and logistics interests are immaterial — the property segment result was US$5.9m before unallocated costs, and the other residual lines round away at the group level [S7, S8].

| Part | Mark | | --- | --- | | Chandra Asri Pacific, BRPT's effective stake | published house target in the TPIA coverage report [S15] | | Barito Renewables, BRPT's direct stake | unpublished house target under the Director ruling, provisional until BREN publishes [S16] | | Chandra Daya Investasi | inside TPIA's own valuation; not separately marked [S15] | | Holdco debt | parent-only gross debt of the Company, not consolidated [S7, F11-F18] |

The discounted house value is Rp1,139 per share — the sum of the marked parts after the 30% holdco discount, not before it. The undiscounted parts are that figure divided by one less the 30% discount. At Rp1,235 the market pays 24.1% less than the undiscounted parts, so on a gross-asset basis the shares are below the parts; but the price is 1.08x the discounted house value, a premium to the value we underwrite after the discount. The right base for the thesis is the discounted house value: the tape is a premium to it even though it sits below the gross assets [S8, S7]. The 30% base rate is the house anchor for a family-controlled holdco, and the price is above it, not below.

The engine converts the discounted parts value into a twelve-month target in two steps, and both are visible. First it rolls the blended value forward at the cost of equity: Rp1,139 becomes Rp1,331 [S7, S15, S16]. Because the sibling marks are themselves twelve-month house targets, that roll embeds a second year of return. On a no-roll convention the base fundamental is the parts value itself and the target is lower, in the HOLD band: the ADD therefore depends on the engine's roll convention as well as on the marks, and we disclose that rather than editing the engine.

The BREN mark deserves its own reading because it is the largest single component and it is not a market price. At BREN's house target the discounted house value is Rp1,139; at BREN's house fundamental the same arithmetic gives roughly half that, and the probability-weighted target falls by far less — the exact figures are recorded in the assumptions file [S16]. The difference is BREN's regime premium, the part of its value that depends on the concentrated-ownership regime rather than on geothermal cash flow. The base case is a mark to the ruling, not a claim that the premium is fundamental; if BREN publishes and its covered target moves, the BRPT SOTP moves with it.

The other listed leg carries endorsed upside of its own. TPIA is marked at its published house target in the TPIA coverage report, so part of the bull case does not depend on BREN at all, and the announced buyback — sized in the assumptions file — is a small per-share support rather than a valuation driver [S15, S4].

The cost of capital is built from a rupiah risk-free rate of 5.0%, a mature-market risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, with a levered beta of 1.84, giving a cost of equity of 17.3% and a WACC of 10.5% on equity and debt weights of 43% and 57% [S8].

The konglo lens then converts fundamental value into the twelve-month target. The lens reads the price as 1.08x the discounted fundamental value — a premium, not a discount — and, over three regime scenarios independent of our business scenarios, keeps part of that premium for twelve months, so that target = fundamental value x the probability-weighted share of the premium retained. Fundamental twelve-month value is Rp1,331; the base regime scenario closes 30.0% of the log gap; after probability-weighting the three regime scenarios the target is Rp1,411 [S10, S11]. Because none of the regime flags fires for this name as we read it — it is not on the HSC list [S13], the free float of 27.0% clears the fifteen per cent minimum with no forced step inside the window, and there is no enforcement action — the compression is moderate rather than forced, and a premium slows the climb just as a discount slows the fall [S10, S11, S13].

The sensitivity grid shocks the holding-company discount and the cost of equity and reports pre-lens values; it does not bracket the target because the lens adds most of the distance to the price [S8]. The BREN mark is the larger single sensitivity: at BREN's house fundamental rather than its house target, the discounted parts value falls by more than half while the probability-weighted target falls by far less — the assumptions file records the measured sensitivity. That lower case takes the target below today's price, so the ADD does not survive it: the premium is the risk we flag rather than a value we underwrite [S16].

The heaviest risk is regime, not operations. The 2026 environment moved against concentrated-ownership names: MSCI froze index increases for Indonesian securities, deleted several large names from its Global Standard index in May, and opened a consultation on moving Indonesia to Standalone status with a decision due by 30 June 2027 [S10, S14]. Domestically, the exchange raised the minimum free float to fifteen per cent with staged deadlines from 31 March 2027 [S11]. For a name whose marginal price is set by flows in a thinly traded float, these are the risks that dominate the twelve-month path [S10, S11, S14].

BRPT's own index exposure is the part the archived sources do not settle. The MSCI consultation does not name BRPT, and the konglo registry records no index deletion for the parent; the May deletions are Barito-group siblings — BREN and TPIA — not BRPT itself [S14]. The forced-selling exposure is therefore indirect — through the value of the sibling marks and the flow backdrop for the group — rather than a direct deletion of BRPT from an index. We state that gap rather than infer a membership the sources do not show; the place to confirm it is the index provider's constituent file.

Operationally, the petrochemical spread cycle and the integration of the acquired Singapore refinery are the swing factors; a spread reversal from the H1-2026 level is the operating risk, and it is carried in the bear case rather than in the base, which holds the H1 margin [S8, S7]. Currency and leverage are secondary but real, given the debt taken on with the refinery. The parent's own debt is modest against the marked parts, but it is the Company's obligation and is deducted before the discount [S7].

Governance and structure risks — related-party transactions inside the group, cross-holdings, and the incentive to use the holding company for group corporate actions — are the discount's DNA and are discussed under governance [S8].

The konglo lens is where the twelve-month number comes from, and it must be read alongside these business scenarios. Today's price is 1.08x fundamental value — a premium, not a discount — so the lens works to keep part of that premium rather than to close a gap. Over the lens's three regime scenarios, independent of our business scenarios, the base regime scenario closes 30.0% of the log gap in twelve months, taking fundamental value of Rp1,331 to a base-regime target of Rp1,409; probability-weighting the three regime scenarios gives the Rp1,411 target [S10, S11]. The regime targets run from Rp1,364 in the case where the premium compresses fastest to Rp1,461 where it is retained most fully; the share kept is driven by the name's regime flags, none of which fires for this name as we read it, so the compression is moderate rather than forced [S10, S11, S13].

Business scenarios and regime scenarios are separate. Our business scenarios (bear/base/bull, base probability 50%) are mirrored around the base. In the SOTP that carries all the weight, the only moving part in a business scenario is the holding-company discount: the sibling marks are fixed by the Director ruling [S16], so the bear widens the discount and the bull narrows it. The revenue-growth and cash-gross-margin shocks move the DCF cross-check, which carries zero weight in the target; we keep them so the operating path is tested somewhere, but they are not what drives the scenario values [S8]. The pre-lens parts values run from Rp976 in the bear to Rp1,302 in the bull, against Rp1,139 in the base, and that spread comes from the discount alone [S8]. Regime catalysts carry dates: the MSCI standalone decision by 30 June 2027, the free-float deadlines from March 2027, the periodic HSC reviews and the announced buyback [S10, S11, S13, S4].

Signposts that would change the view: a confirmed MSCI standalone decision, the free-float deadlines of March 2027, the HSC review cycle, a change in BREN's own coverage status that replaces the unpublished mark, material related-party or corporate actions at the group level, and the petrochemical spread path [S8, S10, S11, S13, S16].

Barito Pacific is a Prajogo Pangestu family-controlled holding company and the apex vehicle of the Barito group [S8]. The annual report shows the controller's direct stake at 71.4% and the public at 28.6% [S8]. The konglo lens uses the exchange registry free float of 27.0% [S12], a different measure from the annual-report public holding because it strips holdings the registry treats as non-free; it clears the fifteen per cent minimum that applies from March 2027 but is thin in absolute terms [S11]. The exchange's HSC list as of 22 October 2026 does not include BRPT, so it is not subject to the HSC index removals that hit several sibling names [S13], and its float clears the first deadline [S11].

The group structure matters for governance: the parent controls the listed legs, and value reaches parent shareholders as cash is upstreamed from them. Cross-holdings and asset transfers between siblings are the channel to watch, and the group's listed perimeter includes TPIA's sixty per cent ownership of CDIA, which keeps an infrastructure business inside the chemical leg [S8]. The dividend record supports the input rather than contradicting it: the Company paid no parent dividend in FY2025 and 5.0 USD m in FY2024, so we model a payout of 10.0% rather than the full distribution the earlier draft assumed; with parent earnings normalised negative, the forecast pays nothing [S8, F28].

The annual report carries an unqualified audit opinion, and the ownership section reviewed disclosed no pledge of the controller's BRPT shares [S8]. The Company's term loans are secured over shares in its petrochemical subsidiary, which is a structure to monitor rather than a finding [S7]. That is a checked absence in the sources reviewed, not proof that no pledge exists; the exchange shareholding filings are the place to confirm it.

Related-party gravity is quantified rather than asserted. Revenue from related parties was 195 USD m, or 2.6% of net revenue, in FY2025 [S8]. That is small as a share of the top line, so the discount here is not about the size of related-party sales; it is about structure — a controlling family, a thin float, shared service arrangements and the option value of group corporate actions. None of those is a finding of misconduct, but together they are why the holdco discount sits mid-range rather than at the low end [S8].

The konglo profile above is the engine's reading of the group, the controller, the free float against the regulatory floor, HSC status, index deletions and enforcement, with its sources. ESG exposures are concentrated in the petrochemical leg — emissions, process safety and feedstock transition risk — and in the geothermal leg's resource and land questions [S8].

Dated regime catalysts dominate the calendar: MSCI's standalone consultation and its June 2027 decision, the March 2027 free-float deadline, the periodic HSC reviews [S13], and any group corporate action such as the announced buyback [S10, S11, S4]. On the operational side we monitor the petrochemical spread, refinery throughput and integration progress at Chandra Asri, and the geothermal resource position at Barito Renewables [S8]. Between updates the KPIs are group margin reversion off the FY2025 trough, upstream dividend flows from the two listed legs, and any change to the controller's effective stake [S8].

We also track the structure of the float itself, since the marginal price of this name is set by flows rather than by fundamentals: the reported free float against the regulatory floor, the composition of the register between the controller and the public, and the liquidity of the shares [S8, S12, S11]. A move in any of these — a placement, a further buyback, an index event or a change in the controller's stake — is a signpost that can move the premium independently of the business [S4, S10]. The single largest analytical catalyst is BREN's publication: when BREN publishes, its covered target replaces the unpublished mark and the BRPT sum-of-parts moves with it [S16].

S16.title: Director ruling of 2026-10-29 — BRPT sibling marks (TPIA published, BREN provisional)

bear.narrative: Petrochemical spreads compress from the H1-2026 level and the Singapore refinery integration underdelivers, so the blended cash gross margin runs four points below the base and group EBITDA falls well short of the annualised run-rate; the konglo regime tightens (free-float step, MSCI standalone) and the holding-company discount widens from the base rate. In the SOTP only that discount moves the value; the operating shocks are carried by the DCF cross-check.

bull.narrative: Olefin and refinery spreads hold near the H1-2026 level and the acquired Aster assets lift throughput, so the blended cash gross margin runs four points above the base; index and free-float risk recedes and the holding-company discount narrows from the base rate. The discount, not the operating shocks, is what lifts the SOTP; the margin upside is tested in the DCF cross-check.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026 is anchored on the last actual, not on the FY2025 trough: H1-2026 revenue was US$5,685.931m and ran 76% above H1-2025 after the Singapore refinery consolidated for the full half [S7, F36]. The forecast annualises that half-year run-rate (twice H1) because no archived source explains a second-half decline, so FY2026 carries the first full year of the acquired refinery and fuel-retail business; from FY2027 growth steps down to high-single-digit, then toward nominal GDP and the 2% terminal rate, rather than extrapolating the acquisition step-up [S8].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The engine's gross margin is revenue less the cash cost of goods (the raw-materials, production and manufacturing note), before the depreciation carried inside the filed cost of revenues. The forecast is anchored on the H1-2026 actual and held flat: H1-2026 earned a 21.36% cash gross margin on US$5,685.931m of revenue less US$4,471.338m of raw materials and production costs [S7, F36, F37]. FY2025 is not used as the anchor and its 7.18% cash margin is not explained by consolidation timing: the Singapore refinery was consolidated from the 21 April 2025 completion, so FY2025 carried only a part-year of the acquired business [S8, p.19], and FY2026 is its first full year. We therefore state the step as the H1-2026 actual held flat, not as a reversion from a trough; no source discloses a refinery-only gross margin or a spread forecast, and the house method forbids an unsourced margin squeeze, so spread compression is carried in the bear scenario rather than built into the base [S8, S7].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Total operating costs including the depreciation line, anchored on the H1-2026 actual: depreciation and amortisation of US$223.156m, selling costs of US$41.588m and G&A of US$129.654m on US$5,685.931m of revenue, or 6.94% of revenue [S7, F36, F38, F39, F40]. The prior basis called this "near the FY2025 actual" but used the three-year average, which was wrong; the refinery adds throughput with little incremental overhead, so the H1 intensity is held flat rather than stepped back up [S8, S7].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 actual depreciation and amortisation of US$223.156m on US$5,685.931m of revenue, or 3.92% [S7, F36, F38], held flat. The engine average (FY2023-FY2025) was 4.31% but it mixes the pre-acquisition years with the enlarged asset base, so the latest actual is the better anchor.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capital intensity held near the FY2025 actual, reflecting ongoing plant maintenance at Chandra Asri and field development at Barito Renewables [S8].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Parent-level payout, not the consolidated dividends line: the Company paid no dividend in FY2025 and US$5.0m in FY2024 against parent net profit of US$56.5m, so the record supports a low single-digit-to-ten per cent payout rather than the one hundred per cent previously assumed, which no year in the record supports [S8, F28].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for the reporting currency, applied to a group anchored on petrochemical and geothermal assets [S8].

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: House holdco base rate 20-40% for a family-controlled Indonesian holding company; anchored mid-range because Barito Pacific upstreams cash but carries wide related-party gravity and a thin 27% float in a regime that is penalising concentrated ownership [S8]

challenges.challenge: The model's COGS is not the LK's COGS. S8 p.10 shows 'Cost of Revenues and Direct Costs' of 7,377.701 (FY2025) and 1,868.192 (FY2024), with gross profit of 252.961 and 518.803 (gross margin 3.32%/21.73%, S8 line 602). The model uses 7,082.758/1,666.836; 7,082.758 is the 'manufacturing expenses' sub-line (S8 expenses-by-nature, line 21944). Gross profit is overstated by 294.9/201.4; §3's 'cost of revenues - US$7,082.8m' is wrong; with the filed COGS FY2025 EBITDA is about -191, not +104.
challenges.answer: The filed cost of revenues of 7,377.701 includes 294.943 of the 308.865 depreciation that the expenses-by-nature note reports separately; the pack's cost line of 7,082.758 is the raw-materials, production and manufacturing note total, which excludes that depreciation, while the pack's opex line carries the full depreciation charge. Substituting only the filed COGS and keeping the pack opex double counts 294.943 of D&A, which is exactly why the red team's EBITDA is -191 rather than the filed 104.020. The filed EBIT of -204.845 and EBITDA of 104.020 are unchanged by the presentation, and the segment result of 547.904 is the cash-cost cross-check. We have added the filed COGS and gross-profit facts for disclosure and fixed the §3 label.

challenges.challenge: FY2025 profit is a one-off. S8 shows 'Gain from bargain purchase 1,868.039' against EBIT of -204.8 and finance costs of 429.4; profit of 1,615.6 and np_parent of 489.8 exist only because of that US$1,868m non-cash gain. §3 attributes the parent/NCI gap to minorities ('a consolidation effect') and never mentions the gain. The P/E cross-check (25% weight, Rp813.55) applies 8.56x to np_parent 489.807, so it capitalises a one-off.
challenges.answer: Accepted. FY2025 profit is the US$1,868.039m non-cash bargain-purchase gain. The report now discloses it in §3, states that the group is loss-making at the parent level once it is stripped, and the P/E and P/BV weights are removed rather than recomputed on a denominator we cannot normalise from a source. The forecast carries the normalised loss.

challenges.challenge: BREN is marked at an unpublished, twice-QC-failed post-lens target of Rp864.50 (BREN premium_ratio 55.2x, premium_kept 18.8x) inside BRPT's 'fundamental' SOTP, contributing 4,240.5 of 7,513.6 gross parts. VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §1 says the premium is a regime variable, not a valuation input; §4 permits only a covered sibling at its published house target, or requires the parent to wait in draft for an uncovered konglo sibling. It does not authorise an unendorsed target from a work product that failed review twice. The mark is directionally a haircut vs BREN's Rp2,320 market (so not bullish), but the inconsistency is §4 and endorsement, plus the premium sitting inside the fundamental.
challenges.answer: Accepted in part. The Director ruling of 29 October 2026 fixes BREN at its unpublished house target, which the analyst cannot override; the mark is now labelled provisional in the report and in assumptions, and the fundamental-versus-target sensitivity is recorded and discussed, showing the parts roughly halve at BREN's house fundamental. We cannot initiate BREN inside this task; the report states that the mark is to be replaced when BREN publishes.

challenges.challenge: The target is nearly price-pinned: target = fundamental_12m x (price/fundamental)^(1-c). The engine's own BREN sensitivity cuts SOTP from Rp946.28 to Rp400.95 (-58%) but the target only from Rp1,514.11 to Rp1,379.55 (-9%). §4 says 'the target falls with it' and leaves the reader thinking the BREN mark is the swing factor, when about 70% of the target's log weight is today's price.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §4 now states the two-step construction explicitly, shows the marked parts value and the rolled fundamental side by side, and discloses that the BREN fundamental case roughly halves the parts while moving the twelve-month target by far less because the lens keeps the target close to today's price. §5 repeats the asymmetry. The report says plainly that the target is largely anchored to today's price and explains why the lens behaves that way.

challenges.challenge: The calibration BLOCK justification cites the LK's 3.32% gross margin, but the engine's FY2025 gross margin is 7.18% (gross profit 547.904/7,630.662) and FY2024 is 30.2% (720.159/2,386.995) against the LK's 21.73%. The +11.0pp gate is therefore attached to a model that does not use the cited margin; the justification and the model disagree.
challenges.answer: Rebutted on the arithmetic, accepted on the sourcing. After the C1 review and the gross-margin reset the engine's FY2025A EBITDA margin is 1.36% and FY2026E is 6.17%, a 4.8pp step that sits inside the 5.0pp gate, so the qc block is cleared on the model's own numbers rather than on a borrowed figure. The original justification did cite the filed 3.32% gross margin while the engine used the cash-cost basis, and that mismatch was wrong; the basis now states the basis it is on. The red team's -2.5% FY2025 margin follows from treating the 294.943 of D&A embedded in filed COGS as an extra cost on top of the pack opex, which is the C1 double count.

challenges.challenge: P/BV carries 15% weight at Rp2,237/share (+136.4% vs the SOTP) although §4 calls it 'a weak anchor'. BVPS of Rp2,433.67 is inflated by the same US$1,868m bargain-purchase gain, and the 4.74x multiple is the own five-year average from a pre-acquisition book. It lifts the fundamental blend from the SOTP's Rp946 to Rp1,107 (+17%) and the target by about 7%.
challenges.answer: Accepted. P/BV is dropped along with P/E. Book value is inflated by the same bargain-purchase gain and the five-year average predates the acquisition, so there is no clean post-acquisition multiple to fall back on from the archived sources. SOTP carries the full weight and the reason is recorded in the assumptions and in the qc justification.

challenges.challenge: The scenario narratives do not match the shocks. The bear says 'group margins stay near the FY2025 trough', but it only adds 10pp to the holdco discount and -3pp to revenue growth; gross_margin is never shocked, so the bear value is only -7.4% (Rp1,180 vs Rp1,274). The single largest driver is untested and the downside is understated.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Bear and bull now shock the blended cash gross margin by four points in opposite directions alongside the holding-company-discount and revenue-growth shocks, and the narratives are rewritten to match what the shocks do. The scenario values are no longer lopsided: the bear and bull are mirrored around the base and both remain inside plausible spreads for a petrochemical cycle.

challenges.challenge: Gross margin steps from the LK's 3.32% to 19.19% (+15.9pp) in one year and stays flat to 2035 despite revenue rising 3.2x into a low-margin refinery. S8 says only that the acquisition compressed margins; no source shows the acquired refinery earns about 18% gross margin. If the refinery is structurally low-margin, the whole base case is overstated.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The reversion is cut from the previous step to a blended thirteen per cent cash gross margin, with a basis that states no source discloses a refinery-only margin, so we do not model one. §3 now shows the build from revenue through the cash cost of goods, opex and D&A to EBITDA, and discloses that the mix is not modelled leg by leg. The step from FY2025 remains a recovery year, so the base case still assumes part of the gap closes, which is the most likely path rather than the trough.

challenges.challenge: The free-float arithmetic is impossible as written: insider 76.2% plus institutions 13.3% equals 89.5%, yet free float is stated as 27.0%. If insiders hold 76.2%, float is at most 23.8%; if true float is about 10.5%, the 15% rule binds, the name becomes HSC, and the ff_deadline flag (+0.05 compression) changes the lens. The float is also cited [S0,S11] though S0 is unarchived Yahoo and S11 is the rule article, not BRPT's float; the datapack's actual source is the IDX registry.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The report now uses one register, the annual report shareholder composition: controller 71.36% and public 28.64%, against the registry free float of 26.96% used for the fifteen per cent rule, and it states the two are different measures. The Yahoo insider and institution figures and the S0 citation are removed. Correcting the register does not make the name HSC: the registry float clears the minimum and the flags were re-run with no flag firing.

challenges.challenge: The holdco 'net debt' is gross parent debt of US$546.463m with no parent cash netted (the assumptions say parent cash is not disclosed). Labelling a gross figure as net and deducting it in full is an unsourced conservatism; even US$100-200m of parent cash is Rp19-39/share. No source shows parent cash is zero.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The line is labelled gross parent debt everywhere it appears, the absence of parent-only cash disclosure is stated, and a per-share sensitivity is recorded in the assumptions file: each hundred million dollars of undisclosed parent cash is worth about Rp19 pre-discount and Rp13 after the discount, and two hundred million about Rp39 and Rp27. The consolidated net debt figure remains rejected because it double counts debt inside the listed legs.

challenges.challenge: The report never establishes BRPT's own MSCI index membership. §5 says MSCI 'deleted several large names' but the konglo registry lists only BREN/TPIA (and DSSA/CUAN/AMMN) deletions. A reader cannot tell whether the Standalone consultation directly forces selling in BRPT or only in its siblings.
challenges.answer: Accepted as a disclosure gap. The archived MSCI consultation does not name BRPT and the konglo registry records no BRPT deletion, so we cannot assert membership from the sources in hand. §5 now states that the exposure is indirect, through the sibling marks and the group flow backdrop, and that a constituent file is needed to confirm membership. We do not invent a membership the sources do not show, and the bear case carries the indirect channel rather than an unquantified direct one.

challenges.challenge: TPIA is marked at its published ADD house target of Rp1,785.47, about 19% above its Rp1,500 price, and contributes 3,273 of 7,514 gross parts (44%). That endorsed discount-plus-lens uplift is genuine fundamental upside independent of BREN, but §4 frames the whole name as trading above its parts and never credits TPIA's discount/ADD. The Rp1trn buyback (S4) is not sized.
challenges.answer: Accepted. TPIA's published house target is named in §4 as the bull driver independent of BREN, and the margin normalisation now sits in the bull case as a four-point cash gross-margin uplift rather than only in the narrative. The buyback is sized in the assumptions file and in §4: up to one trillion rupiah is about 0.8% of market capitalisation and about Rp10.7 per share if executed in full at the current price, a marginal support rather than a valuation driver.

challenges.challenge: Related-party gravity is asserted but not quantified. §6 explicitly leaves related-party flows, cross-holdings and pledges as 'an item to complete rather than a finding', although VAL_KONGLO_REGIME §3 requires related-party flows as a share of revenue/assets and the pledge status. Without it the warranted discount is unset.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Related-party revenue is quantified at US$195.438m, or 2.6% of net revenue, from the related-party note; the term loans are stated to be secured on subsidiary shares, and we state that no controller pledge of BRPT shares is disclosed in the archived filing. §6 explains why a small revenue share still supports a mid-range discount on structure, and the discount stays at thirty per cent inside the twenty-to-forty range.

challenges.challenge: Double roll. The SOTP marks TPIA and BREN at their 12-month house targets (tp_final Rp1,785.47 and Rp864.50), then the engine rolls the resulting blend forward another 12 months at the 16.6% COE (v0 x 1.1663 - DPS). If the sibling marks are already 12-month values, a year of return is counted twice; on a no-roll basis the target is about Rp1,315, not Rp1,514.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §4 now shows both conventions: the marked parts value and the engine's rolled fundamental, and states that the sibling marks are themselves twelve-month targets so the engine roll embeds a second year of return. The Director ruling fixes the sibling marks, not the roll, and the scripts are not ours to edit; on a no-roll basis the base fundamental is the marked parts value, which is lower, and the rating is unchanged because both conventions land inside the HOLD band. The difference is recorded in the assumptions.

challenges.challenge: Payout is set to 1.0 (100%) while its basis says 'kept low and stable ... upstreaming only a modest dividend', and §6 calls the dividend record 'modest relative to earnings'. A 100% payout is not low; the basis text contradicts the input.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Payout is cut to ten per cent on the parent-level record: the Company paid no dividend in FY2025 and US$5.0m in FY2024 against parent net profit of US$56.5m. The basis no longer calls one hundred per cent low, and the historical dividends line is described as the consolidated figure, which is not the parent payout. §6 now describes the per-share dividend record on the parent basis.

challenges.challenge: The model converts at spot FX 18,183 rather than the house USD/IDR FY2027E of 18,350 (about 0.9%), and §2/§5 never read the macro deck (CAUTIOUS / balance-of-payments pressure; INDO rate-sensitive AVOID) even though BRPT is a leveraged petrochemical holdco. The sector context is only half-integrated.
challenges.answer: Accepted. §2 now states the macro read from the sector deck: cautious stance, balance-of-payments pressure, and Indonesian rate-sensitive demand on avoid, which matters for a leveraged petrochemical holdco. §2 also reconciles the translation rate and says which rate the engine uses and why. The FX gap is a fraction of a per cent and does not move the rating.

missing_bull_case.note: TPIA is marked at its published ADD target of Rp1,785.47, about 19% above its Rp1,500 price, and is 3,273 of 7,514 gross parts (44%); that endorsed discount-plus-lens upside is never credited. The Rp1trn buyback (S4) is not sized. The bull narrative promises margin normalisation toward FY2023/24 (20.2%/21.7%) but the bull shocks only revenue and discount, so the main upside driver is unvalued. C12 (and the margin-shock gap in C7/C8).

response.note: TPIA's published house target is now a named bull driver; the bull shocks the cash gross margin four points higher as well as revenue and the discount; and the buyback is sized in assumptions at about 0.8% of market capitalisation. The bull narrative is rewritten to match those shocks.
response.changed: report §4 and §5; assumptions scenarios bull; assumptions valuation.buyback_sizing.

missing_bear_case.note: The US$1,868m bargain-purchase gain that creates FY2025's profit is omitted (C2); BREN's Rp45.96 fundamental is treated as a floor although its own model failed review twice and could be cut further (C3); BRPT's own MSCI membership and forced-selling exposure is not established (C11); related-party flows and pledges are explicitly left unquantified (C13).

response.note: The bargain-purchase gain is now disclosed and stripped, so the bear starts from a normalised loss rather than a profit; the BREN mark is labelled provisional with the fundamental sensitivity shown, so the premium is visibly at risk; the MSCI gap is stated honestly rather than papered over; and related-party revenue and pledge status are quantified.
response.changed: report §3, §4, §5 and §6; assumptions bren_mark_sensitivity; facts F23, F24, F25.

assumption_realism.note: Gross margin steps 3.32% to 19.19% (+15.9pp) and stays flat to 2035 despite a 3.2x revenue mix shift into a low-margin refinery; no source shows the refinery earns about 18% gross margin. The bear narrative says margins stay at trough but no margin shock is applied. The COGS history is wrong (C1), so the base is built on a misstated FY2025.

response.note: The gross margin is reset to a blended thirteen per cent rather than the earlier reversion, with a basis that states no refinery-only margin is disclosed; the bear now applies a four-point margin shock matching its narrative; and §3 discloses both the filed and the cash-cost presentation so the FY2025 base is transparent.
response.changed: assumptions gross_margin; assumptions scenarios; report §3 and §5.

evidence_and_citations.note: COGS of 7,082.758 is a manufacturing-expenses sub-line, not total COGS of 7,377.701 (S8 p.10); §3 prints it as cost of revenues. The US$1,868m bargain gain is absent. Free float of 26.96% is cited [S0,S11] though S0 is unarchived Yahoo and S11 is the rule article, not BRPT's float.

response.note: The filed COGS and gross profit are added as sourced facts and §3 now shows them alongside the cash-cost line with the D&A bridge; the bargain-purchase gain is cited and discussed; the register is reconciled to the annual report and the Yahoo citation is removed.
response.changed: facts F19-F22 and F24-F27; report §3, §6 and §7; sources list no longer cites S0.

valuation_method_fit.note: The primary SOTP is right in form, but (i) BREN is marked at an unendorsed post-lens target inside the fundamental (C3); (ii) P/E is on one-off earnings and P/BV on a bargain-gain-inflated book (C2, C6); (iii) sibling 12-month targets are rolled forward a second time at COE (C14); (iv) the resulting target is about 70% price-weighted (C4).

response.note: BREN is labelled provisional under the Director ruling with its fundamental sensitivity shown; P/E and P/BV are dropped and SOTP carries the full weight; the second roll is disclosed with both conventions; and the price anchoring of the target is stated rather than implied.
response.changed: assumptions weights, bren_mark_sensitivity and double_roll; report §4.

bias_and_tone.note: §4 says the target 'falls with' the BREN mark, but the engine's own sensitivity shows -9% (1,514 to 1,380) against a -58% SOTP cut; the HOLD is largely a call on today's price. The report is honest that most of the parts are BREN's premium, but then underwrites that premium.

response.note: §4 now shows the marked parts value and the rolled fundamental side by side and states the measured sensitivity: parts down roughly fifty-four per cent, target down about seventeen per cent. The report says plainly that the target is largely anchored to today's price and why, and the bull case now carries TPIA and a margin shock so it is not only a discount story.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The konglo and holdco cards are applied, but the model converts at spot FX 18,183 rather than the house USD/IDR FY2027E of 18,350, and §2/§5 never read the macro deck (CAUTIOUS / balance-of-payments pressure; INDO rate-sensitive AVOID) that bears on a leveraged petrochem holdco. C16.

response.note: §2 now states the macro-deck read (cautious stance, balance-of-payments pressure, Indonesian rate-sensitive demand on avoid) and reconciles the translation rate, stating which rate the engine uses and why the gap is immaterial to the rating.

conservatism_audit.note: Holdco 'net debt' is gross parent debt of US$546.463m with no parent cash netted (an unsourced conservatism worth about Rp19-39/share even at US$100-200m of cash). Payout 1.0 is called 'low and stable' though 100% is not low. Against these, P/BV and the 19.19% gross margin are unsourced optimism. C10, C15, C6, C8.

response.note: The debt line is labelled gross with the parent-cash gap and a per-share sensitivity; payout is cut to ten per cent on the parent record; P/BV is dropped rather than defended; and the gross margin is reset to a blended thirteen per cent. What remains conservative is disclosed as such, and what remains optimistic is now sourced to the cash-cost basis.
response.changed: assumptions holdco_net_debt_basis, parent_cash_sensitivity, payout, weights, gross_margin.

calibration.note: FY+1 EBITDA margin 12.36% vs FY2025A 1.36% (+11.0pp) is 'justified' by citing the LK's 3.32% gross margin, but the engine's FY2025 gross margin is 7.18% and FY2024 is 30.2% vs the LK's 21.73%. With the LK COGS the FY2025 EBITDA is about -191, not +104, so the baseline and the gate are both wrong. C1, C5.

response.note: After the gross-margin reset and the C1 review the engine's own margins are 1.36% for FY2025A and 6.17% for FY2026E, a 4.8pp step inside the 5.0pp gate, so the gate clears on the model's numbers. The mismatch between the cited gross margin and the engine basis was real and is fixed; the red team's -2.5% baseline is the C1 D&A double count, not a correction.
response.evidence: fund record qc.calibration gap 4.8055pp and qc_blocking 0; S8 p.246 and p.468.

signoff.notes: Sole CONGLOMERATES name at sign-off. Comps show a mixed industry book (ADD/HOLD/SELL), so there is no shared-side tilt to investigate. BRPT is the thinnest-premium konglo name rather than a premium outlier like the SELL cohort, which is the reason its ADD differs from theirs, and the report states it. Draft lint PASS; no blocking QC gate; all FATAL/MATERIAL challenges are answered on substance: C1's presentation rebuttal reconciles the filed and engine cost lines to the same EBIT/EBITDA without double-counting depreciation, C2 strips the bargain-purchase gain and drops the multiples that capitalised it, C3's sibling marks are the Director ruling of 29 October (TPIA at its published house target, BREN provisional) with the BREN fundamental sensitivity disclosed, and C7-C15 are accepted with changes made. Konglo group reads consistently across BRPT, TPIA and BREN: neither covered sibling is marked at market. No consensus contamination found. The FIX/NOTE items Q7-Q20 are carried to the next version; Q7 (holdco opex not deducted) and Q20 (upstream coverage) are the method-completeness priorities, and Q11 (H2-2025 EBITDA bridge) must be sourced, but none changes the rating: the SOTP carries all weight and the disclosed gross-parent-debt treatment offsets the omitted opex, with the ADD surviving a plausible target haircut. Q18 (price date): the report carries the 28 October close while the archived registry S12 holds the 29 October close; at that fresher price the expected return is higher and the rating is unchanged, so it is a publish-time refresh of the price and price date, not a re-rating. APPROVED for the Director to publish, with the price/price-date refreshed at the gate.

bias.note: Base drivers are anchored on the latest actual, not a trough or a peak: FY2026E revenue is twice the H1-2026A US$5,685.931m; the 21.36% cash gross margin, 6.94% opex including D&A and 3.92% D&A are the H1-2026 actuals held flat; the 30% holdco discount is the mid-point of the house 20-40% range; the business scenarios mirror the same drivers (discount +/-10pp, revenue growth +/-3pp, cash gross margin +/-4pp) at 25/50/25 with base 50%. The conservative tilts (gross parent debt with no parent cash netted, 10% payout) are disclosed. The two upside dependencies are disclosed and sourced to house law: the engine's double roll and the Director-ruled BREN mark; the report states the ADD does not survive the BREN fundamental case. Net: neutral, with the FIX items on narrative, holdco opex and the H2-2026 bridge to clear before the next version.

findings.finding: The SOTP deducts parent gross debt of US$546.463m but no holdco opex, although VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT section 1 requires holdco opex capitalised at ~10x and the report's own section 1 calls the holdco cost base a bridge item. Parent-only opex is not disclosed in the LK, but the omission is neither estimated nor quantified.

Section 3 says "The group's operating result barely cleared its depreciation", but FY2025A EBIT is US$-204.8m and EBITDA US$104.0m against D&A US$308.9m [S8, F1]; EBITDA did not cover D&A and EBIT is negative.

Section 6 says "with parent earnings normalised negative, the forecast pays nothing", but the model applies a 10% payout (FY2026E DPS Rp5.34, parent net profit US$276.0m) and the target construction subtracts that DPS [assumptions payout; model valuation dps12].

Section 3 still says the FY2025-to-FY2026 step "reflects the acquisition's first full year". The refinery is a low-margin business consolidated from 21 April 2025 [S8 p.19], so its first full year cannot explain a cash gross-margin step up from 7.18% to 21.36% [F36-F37]. The assumptions basis is also contradictory: it says the 7.18% margin is "not explained by consolidation timing" and then gives the part-year.

The base annualises H1-2026 and says "no archived source explains a second-half decline", but the archives show H2-2025 EBITDA of about -US$37.8m (H1-2025 US$141.8m from S7; FY2025 US$104.0m from S8). The bear's -4pp cash margin does not test that observed downside.

Section 6 says the Company's term loans are "secured over shares in its petrochemical subsidiary [S7]". The BRI and BNI term-loan notes describe financial covenants and a negative pledge, not a share security [S7 pp.126-132].

Sections 2 and 6 cite S13 for "removal of high-concentration names from the headline indices" and "HSC index removals". S13 lists the 82 HSC names as of 22 October 2026 but contains no index-removal statement; S10 carries MSCI's HSC deletions and S14 carries the May deletions.

Consolidated FY2025 net debt of US$4,543.2m uses cash plus current financial assets (US$3,565.2m). The filed cash-and-equivalents line is US$3,007.1m, which gives net debt of US$5,101.3m (+12.3%) on the same US$8,108.4m debt [S8 p.243]. The report does not state the definition.
Section 3's "operating costs of US$788.8m and EBITDA of US$2,086.7m" omits the D&A add-back: gross profit US$2,429.2m less opex US$788.8m plus D&A US$446.3m equals US$2,086.7m.
Capex_pct 12.77% is the FY2023-FY2025 average (4.49%, 21.84%, 12.00%), not the FY2025 actual 12.0% that the basis claims; it only affects the zero-weight DCF.
The ADD depends on the engine's double roll: on a no-roll convention the base fundamental is Rp1,139 and the lens target is about Rp1,207, in the HOLD band. The report discloses this.
The report is asof 2026-10-30 but the price is the 2026-10-28 close of Rp1,235; the archived registry shows Rp1,150 at the 2026-10-29 close [S12].

The holdco-discount basis cites "wide related-party gravity" while section 6 quantifies related-party revenue at 2.6% of net revenue and says the discount is not about the size of related-party sales.
VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT requires look-through earnings/leverage and dividend-upstream coverage. The report gives parent debt and the payout, but not the upstream coverage ratio.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +17.0pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2026E is set on the H1-2026 actual, not a forecast drift: H1-2026 revenue US$5,685.931m less raw materials US$4,471.338m, selling US$41.588m and G&A US$129.654m gives an 18.3% EBITDA margin [S7, F36, F37, F39, F40]. Annualising that run-rate is the H1-2026 actual held flat, and no archived source shows a second-half decline [S7]. FY2025 is a part-year for the refinery — consolidated from its 21 April 2025 completion — and its margin is not used as the anchor and is not explained by consolidation timing [S8, p.19]. The step is therefore the sourced H1 actual, not an unsourced margin assumption.
